title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed. We reconcile estimand algebra, expand execution/accounting and reproducibility details, add an explicit primary verification citation, and provide cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths for forensic verification.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. However, incorrect or out-of-order commands can cause outages or violate workflow policies; production proposals therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Despite intuitive appeal, rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract is scarce and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our principal contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired confirmatory estimand and analysis pipeline with preserved cryptographic artifact digests; (2) a conservative adapter contract enforcing a shared initial generation and a single automated repair attempt; and (3) full archival of per-episode deterministic validator traces, canonical ASTs, and analysis artifacts enabling deterministic audit of contingency cells and the single discordant episode.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network verification methods and runtime validators underpin many practical NetOps guardrails. A canonical technical foundation is the Header Space Analysis static-check framework (Kazemian, Varghese, McKeown, "Header space analysis: static checking for networks", 2012; primary source archived in the evidence bundle). Incremental and online checkers such as VeriFlow (Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452) extend static checks to staged updates. Recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (NetConfEval; Lira et al.) focus on generation accuracy and emergent failure modes but often omit preregistration, shared‑initial paired designs, or forensic artifact manifests. Generate–validate–repair studies demonstrate verifier-assisted self-correction but vary widely in repair budgets and whether baseline and guarded outputs share initial candidates. Our work complements these by combining deterministic validator traces and strict adapter budgeting with preregistered paired inference and archived cryptographic artifact digests to attribute any marginal benefit unambiguously to the guarded repair action.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design (N=200) stratified across planned vendor families (Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67) and defined the primary_estimand as the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The confirmatory test was the exact McNemar two-sided test; we also specified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Full preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4.

Adapter contract and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1, requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation (one initial candidate reused by baseline and guarded) and permitted at most one automated repair per task. Provider-call accounting is archived (execution/execution_manifest.json; deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891).

Synthetic task bank, deterministic validator, and scoring. The task bank (deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5) emits explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies, and required_sequence for each task. The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) parses model outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax/parse, applies intent-constraint and dependency checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. The validator returns per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and a binary score using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs and raw responses are archived under execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ (see Disclosure for SHA-256 digests). The analysis pipeline (paired_binary_analysis_v1) consumed execution/raw_results.jsonl and produced contingency counts and bootstrap CI; all analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 digests.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

Per-vendor summary and location of the discordant episode. The preregistered stratification was Cisco-like: N=66; Juniper-like: N=67; RFC-neutral: N=67; execution produced complete_pair_count = 200 with no deterministic exclusions, so observed per-stratum sample sizes equal the preregistered plan (66/67/67). The overall contingency counts above (n_11=199,n_10=1,n_01=0,n_00=0) show exactly one baseline failure that was corrected by the single recorded repair (stage_counts repair = 1). The precise per-vendor decomposition of baseline/guarded successes and the exact episode identifier (the pair id of the single discordant episode) are deterministically recorded in the archived execution artifacts: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02). Auditors can extract the episode id and per-vendor counts exactly from those files and from the corresponding per-episode scoring JSON in execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json). We provide these artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests so readers can deterministically reproduce the per-vendor table and identify the single discordant episode; the authoritative source of the verbatim episode id and its scoring-JSON SHA-256 is execution/raw_results.jsonl and the per-episode JSON under execution/scoring/, both archived with the SHA-256s above.

Provider-call accounting and repair diagnostics. Provider_call_audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. This explains model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair). The unique repair_applied = true episode is traceable via the per-episode scoring JSON (execution/scoring/) and the raw_results manifest (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 above). Missingness_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 808b3c00...) shows zero failed provider calls and zero deterministic exclusions.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation and statistical perspective. The guarded pipeline converted the single observed actionable error into a valid configuration under the constrained execution contract, but the baseline failure prevalence was exceptionally low (1/200). The exact McNemar two-sided p-value (p = 1.0) and bootstrap CI ([0.0, 0.015]) reflect the paucity of discordant information: with only one discordant pair the two-sided exact test is noninformative. Consequently the preregistered power calibration (targeting large absolute reductions ≈0.15) is not applicable here; the study was underpowered to make confirmatory claims about large absolute-effect targets in a very-rare-failure regime. Decision-theoretic practice in rare-failure regimes should favor cost-weighted estimands or targeted stress sampling rather than sole reliance on proportion tests.

Operational implications. Marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the cost of undetected errors. In workloads with extremely low baseline error rates, expensive validators or broad automation may have small average benefit though they can prevent occasional costly incidents. Conversely, higher baseline-error workloads or those where single failures are catastrophic will justify more extensive validator coverage and larger repair budgets. Our controlled run demonstrates that a GVR guard can eliminate an observed actionable error but does not alone quantify deployment-level cost–benefit tradeoffs.

Design lessons. To evaluate validator impact when baseline failures are rare, researchers should: (a) increase N or oversample high-difficulty strata to increase discordant mass; (b) adopt stratified or targeted stress tasks emphasizing 'very_hard' patterns to expose validator boundaries; (c) consider cost-weighted estimands that up-weight catastrophic outcomes; and (d) explore expanded repair budgets (multiple automated repairs) to measure diminishing returns. The archived per-episode validator_traces enable automated clustering of residual violation codes to guide targeted validator improvements in future runs.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment assessing a deterministic-validator guard in an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). Because baseline failures were extremely rare, the preregistered large-effect confirmatory claim (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported. We supply cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths (preregistration SHA-256; execution and analysis artifact SHA-256s) so auditors can deterministically reconstruct contingency cells, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the archived evidence. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures to inform deployment decisions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are deterministically retrievable from archived artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl and execution/raw_results.jsonl) and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ but are not reproduced verbatim in this narrative to preserve artifact-first forensic traceability (artifact SHA-256s above allow exact retrieval).
